findings.title: Unify outcome and proof input_ref hash bases in the bundle
findings.body: Within one bundle outcome, outcome.input_ref is canonical_input_hash(Website model) (e.g. 37de1428…) while source_proof.input_ref and every observation's input_ref are canonical_input_hash(url string) (ab64b5ed…), because scrape_websites→_scan_occurrences hashes the typed source object while admit_fetch/extract_observations hash the URL value. A consumer joining outcomes to observations or proofs by input_ref gets zero matches and must fall back to key/occurrence_id; release_smoke verify only cross-checks observation↔proof (same basis) so it never detects the divergence. Attribution itself remains correct and each basis is deterministic; impact is consumer confusion and a dead join key, observed empirically on c01/bundle.json at 907e94da.

findings.title: Document --request-timeout as the whole-operation deadline
findings.body: ScrapeOptions.request_timeout feeds allocation.elapsed_seconds, which execute_fetch uses both as the per-request httpx timeout and as the overall waiter deadline, and execute_fetch_with_source_proof extends to the capture phase. A serialized batch (3×750ms fixtures, --max-concurrency 1, --request-timeout 2) returned failure/timeout for all inputs including fetches that had already completed under the per-request budget, because deadline expiry during capture retroactively replaces completed-but-uncaptured successes with typed timeouts. Behavior is conservative (no false success, resources retained) but the flag name and README imply per-request semantics, so large or serialized batches fail unexpectedly at the default 10s.

findings.title: Handle relative --work-dir in release_smoke run
findings.body: release_smoke.py run with a relative --work-dir fails during build_and_install: uv export runs with cwd=source while -o receives the still-relative requirements path, so the subsequent uv pip install reports "File not found: ../smoke/work/requirements.txt" and the harness exits 3 without running any case. Reproduced at 907e94da with --work-dir ../smoke/work; an absolute path works. DEF-24's documented command does not require an absolute path, so a reviewer following it can misread the gate as broken.

findings.title: Byte cap charge-then-check allows one-chunk overshoot
findings.body: _Ledger.charge_bytes adds the chunk size before testing the limits, so a response streamed without Content-Length is read up to one transport chunk past max_bytes_per_input before body_too_large is returned: a 2MiB chunked stream against the 1,048,576-byte default was charged 1,081,291 bytes. The outcome stays a typed failure, the overshoot is bounded by a single chunk and is honestly reported in resources.bytes, so this is informational: actual reads can slightly exceed the advertised cap.

findings.title: verify without --python accepts edited report prose
findings.body: release_smoke.py verify validates bundle/jsonl/artifact integrity but only re-renders report.md when --python is supplied; a copy of a good bundle whose report.md was edited to read "verified contacts" still prints VALID in the no-render mode. The tool explicitly prints this limitation and the machine bundle remains tamper-evident (the same edit is caught with --python), so this is informational: consumers of report.md alone should be pointed at the rendered-verification mode.
